html: I'târap is the name on the map for a small area in central Rondônia, Brazil, near the city of Ji-Paraná. Little reliable information about the name is available. It seems to be an Indigenous self-name for a people of this area, which is the land of Tupi-speaking groups such as the Arara (Karo) and Gavião (Ikolen) of the Igarapé Lourdes territory, and close to the Paiter Suruí and the Cinta Larga. These peoples lived in the forest until roads and settlers reached Rondônia in the 1960s and 1970s.
